bookTitle: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis

facts.statement: The distribution phase is the exact opposite of accumulation, representing the campaign where market insiders move prices to retail levels and systematically sell off accumulated inventory to retail buyers.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: The distribution phase is the exact opposite of the accumulation phase... the campaign where insiders move the price higher, to encourage the somewhat nervous and jaundiced buyers back into the market.

facts.statement: Distribution unfolds in two distinct stages: the Natural Phase early on where insiders meet natural retail demand driven by existing trend momentum with above-average volume, and the Selling Climax where insiders actively force prices higher using media hype with ultra-high volume.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: This first phase of distribution, is what I call the 'natural' phase... The final phase is the selling climax, and this is where effort is required by the insiders... forcing it higher, desperately selling in large volume.

facts.statement: While accumulation exploits retail fear of loss, distribution exploits the fear of missing out (FOMO) and greed, causing retail traders to hesitate initially and then buy heavily near the market peak right before reversal.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Whilst the key emotional driver in 'shaking the trees' in the accumulation phase was fear... the key driver that is used in the distribution phase is also fear, but this time the fear of missing out on a good trade.

facts.topic: Up by Stairs Down by Elevator
facts.statement: Coulling compares market cycles to a helter-skelter: markets rise slowly in steps ('up by the stairs') over time to rebuild retail confidence and liquidate inventory, but drop rapidly ('down by the elevator') once warehouses are empty.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Coulling compares market cycles to a fairground helter-skelter... Climbing to the top requires walking up many steps with considerable effort, but sliding down on a mat happens very quickly.

facts.statement: During distribution, public demand peaks due to bullish media coverage under supply/demand; the duration of the sideways range dictates markdown severity under cause/effect; and high volume yielding narrow spreads represents an effort-result anomaly.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Wyckoff's Three Laws... Law of Supply and Demand... Law of Cause and Effect... Law of Effort vs. Result.

facts.statement: Distribution signatures include narrow spread candles with ultra-high volume (insider absorption), shooting stars or deep upper wicks with high volume (early selling/rejection), and topping-out volume arcing patterns.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Narrow Spread Candle + Ultra-High Volume... Shooting Star / Deep Upper Wick... Topping Out Volume.

facts.statement: Before marking prices down sharply, insiders test the market to ensure no residual buying demand remains: a low-volume test confirms exhaustion and permits a rapid markdown, while high volume indicates a failed test requiring further absorption.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Before marking the price down sharply, insiders test the market to ensure no residual buying power (demand) remains... Low Volume Test... High Volume Test.

facts.statement: Insiders utilize the news media similarly to aggressive marketing campaigns (like Acai berry hype), hyping promises of easy wealth to generate emotional retail buying near market tops.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Insiders use the news media like a marketing campaign for Acai berries—hyping the promise of easy wealth to generate emotional retail buying.

facts.statement: The selling climax acts as a dramatic firework display marking the emotional conclusion of the distribution phase, characterized by volatile price surges and heavy volume before the markdown begins.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: The Selling Climax acts as the dramatic 'fireworks show' marking the end of the distribution phase before the market falls.

facts.statement: Large operators face an illiquidity dilemma where they cannot dump their massive inventory in a single block without crashing market prices against themselves, requiring multi-session distribution or dark pools.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Insiders cannot dump their entire inventory in a single order without crashing the market price against themselves. They must spread distribution across multiple sessions or use dark pools.

facts.statement: Citing Richard Ney's work, specialists exploited the panic following President Kennedy's assassination on November 22, 1963, as an alibi to drop stock prices to wholesale levels, such as marking AT&T down from $138 to $130.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Quoting Richard Ney's The Wall Street Gang, specialists used the market panic following JFK's assassination as an alibi to drop stock prices to wholesale levels... Telephone dropped... from $138 to $130.

facts.statement: During the November 22, 1963 panic, the AT&T specialist accumulated inventory at wholesale lows, closed the exchange early, reopened on November 25 at $140, and captured a $25,000 personal trading profit.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: The specialist in Telephone dropped the stock from $138 to $130 on November 22... reopened the stock on Monday, November 25, at $140, capturing $25,000 in personal profit.

facts.statement: Accumulation and distribution cycles are fractal, occurring simultaneously across all timeframes where minor intraday cycles sit inside daily cycles, mirroring nested Russian dolls.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Accumulation and distribution cycles occur across all timeframes simultaneously; a 1-minute cycle sits inside a 5-minute cycle, which sits inside a daily cycle.

generalAssumptions: Market price manipulation is structurally transparent on the volume tape.
Effort versus result governs institutional capital movement.
